posts.author: Tangerenzie
posts.body:
How do you guys usually make your mapa? Do you import it all into RPG Maker as a tileset? Or do you use parallax mapping and plugins, is one of them much easier than the other? Or are they all about the samw... And what programs do you use for making these tiles? Do you all use GIMP or Aseprite? Or are there other options?
Just looking to discuss and learn here

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
You're asking about several different things.
There's no such thing as "import a map into RPG Maker as a tileset".
I assume you've used MV at least a bit, made some maps? That's clearly much easier than drawing the map in an image editor to import it as parallax.
Similarly, most people do not "make" their tiles at all. They use the tilesets included in RPG Maker, the ones available here in the resources section of the forum, and/or the ones you can purchase on various sites.
If you
are
drawing them, I don't think Aseprite is a good choice because it seems to be very focused on creating character sheet frames - but I haven't used it, that's just my impression. I don't think I've seen anyone talk about using it for tiles.
Avery has a bunch of tutorials on how to draw and modify tiles, and she has a few pieces of software she recommends. There are also handfuls of existing threads about this where people recommend various software for specific applications.

posts.author: MushroomCake28
posts.body:
Many people make maps in various different ways, but I think if we had to classify them it would be with the following:
Mapping in RPG Maker with tilesets
Parallax mapping in a third party software (Photoshop, GIMP, etc.)
Drawing/Painting maps
For 1 & 2 people usually use RTP assets, sometimes add DLC tiles, sometimes customize existing assets, and sometimes create new assets.
Artists have greater flexibility since they can paint their maps from scratch and can create assets.
I personally parallax map in GIMP using RTP assets, DLCs, edits, and forum resources.

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
Tangerenzie said:
is one of them much easier than the other?
Click to expand...
This entirely depends on your skill set.  I have seen superb maps made with tiles and dreadful maps done with parallax, as well as vice versa.
If you are new to RPG Maker and game dev in general, I would strongly suggest that you start with mapping with tiles.  That is because you need to learn how to create a good
map
before you start thinking about eye candy.  You need to learn about navigational aspects, how to interest the player, how to create a map for the specific purpose of that map, etc. etc.  It's a lot quicker to do a map with tiles, see your mistakes, change it round, choose other tiles, alter your layout and so on than to have to redo a parallax.
